defects.description: If more than a third of US adults were obese, then a bit under two-thirds were not, but the text says 'fewer than one-quarter were not' obese.
paraphrases: More than a third obese implies almost two-thirds not obese, not fewer than a quarter.
'Fewer than one-quarter not obese' would mean over three-quarters obese, contradicting 'more than a third'.
The obese and non-obese shares do not add up.
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'fewer than two-thirds' (complement of more than a third). Findable from the obese share, distinct.

defects.description: If over 60% of US adults were overweight or obese, then under 40% were at a healthy weight or below, but the text says 'over 40%'.
paraphrases: Over 60% overweight leaves under 40% healthy, not over 40%.
The two shares would exceed 100% (over 60% plus over 40%).
defects.rationale: Correct phrasing 'under 40%' (complement of over 60%). Findable from the overweight share, distinct.

defects.description: The global overweight/obese share is given as 'two-fifths — about 20%', but two-fifths is 40%, not 20%.
paraphrases: Two-fifths is 40%, so 'about 20%' does not match.
The fraction (two-fifths) and the percentage (20%) disagree.
defects.rationale: Correct value 'about 40%' (two-fifths). Findable from the fraction and the figure in the same sentence, distinct.
